cases.title: Authorized text task and resume
cases.assertion: An authorized sender can complete the fixture task, receive a bounded reply, and resume only the documented session.

cases.title: Unauthorized ingress
cases.assertion: An unauthorized sender, channel, thread, webhook, bot, or self-message creates no model input, Run, side effect, or reply.

cases.title: Stable identity
cases.assertion: A matching display name or mutable profile cannot impersonate an authorized immutable platform identity.

cases.title: Replay and duplicate delivery
cases.assertion: Replaying one platform event one hundred times causes at most one writable execution and one logical result.

cases.title: Closed execution authority
cases.assertion: Message content cannot inject or select cwd, host path, image, argv, environment, mount, network policy, credential, runtime, plugin, skill, MCP server, or target revision.

cases.title: Connector compromise containment
cases.assertion: Code execution in the Connector cannot reach any workspace, provider credential, control database, other platform token, executor API, or container-runtime socket.

cases.title: Control-plane compromise containment
cases.assertion: Code execution in the routing control plane cannot access workspace contents, provider credentials, or runtime authority and can request only pre-approved target revisions.

cases.title: Runner confinement
cases.assertion: The Runner sees only approved workspace and state resources and cannot access platform credentials, control databases, host secrets, runtime sockets, or another target or Run.

cases.title: Untrusted repository configuration
cases.assertion: Repository instructions, symlinks, hooks, MCP configuration, plugins, and skills cannot reveal canaries or expand execution authority.

cases.title: Provider-only network path
cases.assertion: Required model traffic succeeds while a model-controlled tool cannot reach the lab collector, arbitrary public internet, LAN, host services, or metadata endpoints unless explicitly approved.

cases.title: Reusable provider credential isolation
cases.assertion: Model-controlled tools cannot recover a reusable provider credential from files, environment, process state, protocol traffic, logs, or persisted session state.

cases.title: Cancellation cleanup
cases.assertion: Cancellation terminates the full process tree and removes the runtime before execution authority or a writable workspace lock is released.

cases.title: Crash and uncertain-create recovery
cases.assertion: Injected crashes at lifecycle boundaries neither duplicate a writable execution nor leave an unowned runtime, stale authority, or prematurely released lock.

cases.title: Session scope
cases.assertion: Resume is scoped to exact identity, conversation, target, and target revision, and opaque vendor session credentials do not enter chat or the routing control plane.

cases.title: Output and evidence redaction
cases.assertion: Replies, logs, errors, and evidence contain no reusable tokens, raw environment, private vendor session identifiers, unsanitized stderr, or host paths.

cases.title: Resource bounds
cases.assertion: CPU, memory, PID count, wall time, output bytes, event count, and persistent disk growth are bounded and observable.
